intro: Every recent Refregier exam closes with a Friedmann-equation problem. In the Expansion Engine you derive how a(t) depends on what fills the universe, date nucleosynthesis, and let a black hole feed at the Eddington rate.

blocks.tex: v=H_0d,\qquad 1+z=\frac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{\lambda_{\rm em}}=\frac{a_0}{a(t_{\rm em})},\qquad v\approx cz\ (z\ll1)
blocks.label: Hubble law and cosmological redshift.

blocks.html: $H_0\approx70$ km s$^{-1}$Mpc$^{-1}$ (often written $100h$ with $h\approx0.7$). Its inverse, the Hubble time $1/H_0=977.8/H_0[\mathrm{km/s/Mpc}]$ Gyr $\approx14$ Gyr, sets the age scale of the Universe.

Redshift is not a Doppler shift through space: the wavelength of light is stretched together with space, $\lambda\propto a$. That is why $1+z$ is exactly the factor by which the Universe has grown since the light left. Every observer sees the same Hubble law (no centre): stretch a rubber sheet with dots on it and every dot sees the others recede with $v\propto d$.

Cosmological principle: on large scales ($\gtrsim100\,h^{-1}$ Mpc) the Universe is homogeneous and isotropic. Then the only freedom is a single scale factor $a(t)$ and a constant spatial curvature $k\in\{-1,0,+1\}$: the Robertson–Walker metric.
$v=cz$ only for $z\ll1$. For $z\sim1$ use $1+z=a_0/a$ and do not quote a velocity. Frequencies: $1+z=\nu_{\rm em}/\nu_{\rm obs}$ (HS25 winter MC14: 1420 MHz seen at 700 MHz is $z\approx1$).

blocks.html: A 2D picture: a sphere (positive curvature, $k=+1$: triangle angles sum to more than 180°, parallel lines meet, finite area), a plane ($k=0$: 180°), a saddle (negative curvature, $k=-1$: less than 180°, infinite).

$\Omega>1$: more than enough mass, space closes on itself like a sphere and (without $\Lambda$) the expansion eventually reverses. $\Omega=1$: flat, the "escape velocity" case. $\Omega<1$: open, expands forever. Observations (CMB) say our Universe is very nearly flat: $\Omega_{\rm tot}=1$ to within ~0.5 %.

Triangle angle sum $>180^\circ$ means positive curvature (HS24 summer MC14), and $\Omega_{\rm tot}>1$ means closed, $k=+1$ (HS25 winter MC15). Never "cylindrical": a cylinder has zero intrinsic curvature.

encounters.title: The Friedmann equation from a Newtonian shell

blocks.html: Take a sphere of radius $a$ in a uniform universe of density $\rho$. A test mass on its surface feels only the mass inside, $M=\frac43\pi a^3\rho$ (shell theorem). Energy conservation: $\frac12\dot a^2-\frac{GM}{a}=E$, i.e. $\dot a^2-\frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho a^2=2E$. General relativity gives the same equation with $2E=-kc^2$ (Choudhuri (10.25)-(10.27)):
How $\rho$ depends on $a$ follows from the first law for an expanding volume $a^3$ with pressure $P=w\rho c^2$: $d(\rho c^2a^3)+P\,d(a^3)=0$:

Matter is diluted ($n\propto a^{-3}$). Radiation is diluted AND each photon is redshifted ($E\propto a^{-1}$): $a^{-4}$. Vacuum energy is a property of space, so it does not dilute. Hence the history: radiation dominated early, matter later (after $z_{eq}\approx3400$), and dark energy today.

Numbers: $\rho_{c,0}=\frac{3H_0^2}{8\pi G}=1.88\times10^{-26}h^2$ kg m$^{-3}$ (10.29), about 5 protons per cubic metre. Today $\Omega_M\approx0.3$, $\Omega_\Lambda\approx0.7$, $\Omega_R\approx9\times10^{-5}$.

$k$ is only a sign ($-1,0,1$); the radius of curvature is in $a$. For $k=0$ the Friedmann equation is just $\dot a/a=\sqrt{8\pi G\rho/3}$: separate variables (exam hint: $a$-terms with $da$ on the left).

blocks.tex: k=0:\quad a\propto t^{\frac{2}{3(1+w)}}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{matter }a\propto t^{2/3},\ \text{radiation }a\propto t^{1/2};\qquad\Lambda:\ a\propto e^{Ht},\ H=\sqrt{8\pi G\rho_\Lambda/3}

blocks.label: Closed universe (cycloid): Big Bang at η = 0, turnaround at η = π, Big Crunch at η = 2π.

blocks.html: Choudhuri Fig. 10.5: $a(t)$ for $k=+1$ rises from zero, bends over and falls back (a cycloid arch); $k=0$ grows as $t^{2/3}$ forever; $k=-1$ grows faster and approaches $a\propto t$ (coasting). All three curves start together at the Big Bang with infinite slope; near $t=0$ curvature does not matter.

Age: for a flat matter universe $H=\frac{2}{3t}$, so $t_0=\frac23H_0^{-1}\approx9.3$ Gyr, younger than the oldest stars (12–13 Gyr): one of the hints that dark energy exists. With $\Lambda$ the expansion accelerates (SN Ia distances, 1998) and the age becomes 13.8 Gyr.

For $H=\alpha/t$ (power law) the age is $\alpha/H$, not $1/H$. In a closed universe the present time must be before turnaround if we see expansion: $t_\odot<t_{\rm ta}$ gives an upper limit on $H_0$ (HS24 winter Q7c).
Every exam ends with Friedmann: radiation era and BBN (HS25 winter Q7), general $w$ (HS24 summer Q7), cosmological constant (HS25 practice Q7), closed universe lifetime (HS24 winter Q7).

encounters.title: Power-law expansion for a fluid with equation of state w
encounters.goal: Flat universe, $\rho=\rho_0(a_0/a)^{3(1+w)}$, $w>-1$. From $(\dot a/a)^2=\frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho-\frac{kc^2}{a^2}$ show $a\propto t^\alpha$ with $\alpha=\frac{2}{3(1+w)}$, and give the matter and radiation cases.

encounters.title: A universe dominated by a cosmological constant
encounters.goal: Flat universe with only dark energy of constant density $\rho_\Lambda$. Show that $H$ is constant and $a\propto e^{Ht}$.

steps.reveal: $H^2=\frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho_\Lambda$: constant in time since $\rho_\Lambda$ is.
$\frac{da}{dt}=aH\Rightarrow d\ln a=H\,dt\Rightarrow a\propto e^{Ht}$, with $H=\sqrt{8\pi G\rho_\Lambda/3}$ in the exponent.

encounters.title: Light from the last scattering
encounters.problem: The CMB temperature today is $T_0=2.725$ K and scales as $T\propto a^{-1}\propto1+z$. Recombination happens at $T_{\rm rec}\approx3000$ K. Wien's constant is $b=2.898\times10^{-3}$ m K.

steps.prompt: Peak wavelength of the radiation at recombination in nm.
Peak wavelength today in mm. (It is stretched by $1+z$.)
steps.hint: Same Wien law at $T_0$, equal to $\lambda_{\rm rec}(1+z)$.

encounters.title: Growing a quasar: the Salpeter time
encounters.problem: A black hole accretes at the Eddington rate with radiative efficiency $\eta=0.1$: $L=\eta\dot M_{\rm acc}c^2$, $\dot M_{BH}=(1-\eta)\dot M_{\rm acc}$, $L_{\rm Edd}=4\pi GM_{BH}m_pc/\sigma_T$. Then $M_{BH}(t)=M_{BH}(0)e^{t/t_S}$ with $t_S=\frac{\eta}{1-\eta}\frac{c\sigma_T}{4\pi Gm_p}$.

steps.prompt: Salpeter time in units of $10^7$ yr.
steps.hint: Insert $G,\,m_p,\,\sigma_T,\,c$ in SI. The result is $5.0\times10^7$ yr.

steps.prompt: Time to grow by a factor $10^8$ (a $10\,M_\odot$ seed to $10^9\,M_\odot$) in Gyr.
steps.hint: $t=t_S\ln(10^8)=18.4\,t_S\approx0.9$ Gyr. This is why $z>7$ quasars are a puzzle.

encounters.title: Friedmann universe with equation of state $w$
encounters.problem: Flat universe with $\rho\propto a^{-3(1+w)}$: $\dot a/a=\sqrt{8\pi G\rho/3}$ gives $a\propto t^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha=\frac{2}{3(1+w)}$. Then $H=\dot a/a=\alpha/t$, so the age is $t_0=\alpha/H_0$. Take $H_0=70$ km/s/Mpc, $1/H_0=13.97$ Gyr.

steps.prompt: Age of a flat matter-only universe $t_0=\alpha/H_0$ in Gyr.
steps.hint: $t_0=\frac23\cdot13.97\,\text{Gyr}\approx9.3$ Gyr (younger than the oldest stars: one reason for $\Lambda$).

encounters.title: Quick fire: Hubble law and the 21 cm line
encounters.problem: A galaxy at redshift $z=0.024$, $H_0=72$ km/s/Mpc, and $v\approx cz$. Separately, the $21$ cm line (rest frequency $1420.4$ MHz) is received at $700$ MHz. Estimate each within about 25 %.

steps.prompt: Redshift of emission of the 21 cm line seen at 700 MHz: $1+z=\nu_{\rm em}/\nu_{\rm obs}$.
steps.hint: Frequencies scale inversely to wavelengths: $1+z=\lambda_{\rm obs}/\lambda_{\rm em}=\nu_{\rm em}/\nu_{\rm obs}\approx2$.
Divide km/s/Mpc by km per Mpc.

steps.prompt: Critical density $3H_0^2/(8\pi G)$ in $10^{-27}$ kg m$^{-3}$.
Equivalent number of protons per m$^3$.
steps.hint: About 5.5: the Universe is very empty.

encounters.title: Life and death of a closed universe
encounters.problem: Matter-only closed universe with $\Omega_{M,0}=2$ and $H_0=70$ km/s/Mpc ($1/H_0=13.97$ Gyr). Use $H_0t=\frac{\Omega_0}{2(\Omega_0-1)^{3/2}}(\eta-\sin\eta)$ (HS24 winter Q7).

steps.prompt: Total lifetime Big Bang to Big Crunch ($\eta=2\pi$) in Gyr.
steps.hint: Symmetric cycloid: twice the turnaround time.

steps.prompt: Age today: today $a=a_0$, so $1-\cos\eta_0=2(\Omega-1)/\Omega=1$, $\eta_0=\pi/2$. Age in Gyr.
steps.hint: $H_0t_0=\frac{2}{2}(\frac\pi2-1)=0.571$: only 8 Gyr, younger than the flat case.

encounters.title: When did matter take over from radiation?
encounters.problem: Use $\rho_\gamma=a_BT_0^4/c^2$ with $T_0=2.725$ K, $a_B=7.566\times10^{-16}$ J m$^{-3}$K$^{-4}$, total radiation $\rho_R=1.68\rho_\gamma$ (photons + neutrinos, Choudhuri (10.47)), and $\rho_M=\Omega_M\rho_c$ with $\Omega_M=0.3$, $\rho_c=9.20\times10^{-27}$ kg m$^{-3}$.

steps.prompt: Photon mass density today in $10^{-31}$ kg m$^{-3}$.
CMB temperature at equality in K.

encounters.title: The far future: a Λ-dominated universe
encounters.problem: When matter has thinned out, only $\rho_\Lambda=0.7\rho_{c,0}$ is left. Then $H_\Lambda=\sqrt{8\pi G\rho_\Lambda/3}=\sqrt{0.7}\,H_0$. Take $H_0=70$ km/s/Mpc.

steps.prompt: Doubling time of the scale factor, $\ln2/H_\Lambda$, in Gyr.

encounters.title: Boss: the radiation-dominated universe (exam problem)

source.where: Open Question 7 [Radiation era and BBN, 12 pt], HS25 winter session

encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer, then enter the final numbers. Parts (a) and (b) are graded by you against the key points.
statement: The early universe was hot, dense and dominated by radiation. Consider a spatially flat ($k=0$) universe containing only radiation.

(a) [4 pt] The energy density of radiation scales as $\rho\propto a^{-4}$. Starting from the Friedmann equation $(\dot a/a)^2=\frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho$, show that $a(t)\propto t^{1/2}$. Assume $a(0)=0$ at $t=0$.
(b) [4 pt] The energy density of blackbody radiation is related to the temperature by $\rho\propto T^4$. Using (a), show that $T(t)\propto t^{-1/2}$.

(c) [4 pt] Big Bang Nucleosynthesis took place when the universe had cooled to $T_{BBN}\approx10^9$ K. Assuming radiation domination throughout, and given $T\approx1.5\times10^{10}$ K at $t=1$ s, estimate the age $t_{BBN}$.

finalAnswers.prompt: Extension: age in minutes when $T=3\times10^8$ K.

keyPoints: (a) $\rho=\rho_0(a_0/a)^4\Rightarrow\dot a/a=C/a^2\Rightarrow a\,\dot a=C\Rightarrow a\,da=C\,dt\Rightarrow a^2=2Ct$ with $a(0)=0$; so $a\propto t^{1/2}$.

encounters.title: Boss: the closed universe (exam problem)
encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer (sketch included), then enter the final numbers.
statement: For a matter-dominated closed universe, the solution of the Friedmann equation is $\frac{a}{a_0}=\frac{\Omega_{M,0}}{2(\Omega_{M,0}-1)}(1-\cos\eta)$, $H_0t=\frac{\Omega_{M,0}}{2(\Omega_{M,0}-1)^{3/2}}(\eta-\sin\eta)$, where $a_0$, $\Omega_{M,0}$ and $H_0$ are the scale factor, matter density parameter and Hubble parameter today, and $\eta$ is the conformal time.
(a) [4 pt] Describe in words the evolution of the closed universe. Sketch $a$ vs $t$. Mark the Big Bang, turnaround and Big Crunch, and give the corresponding values of $\eta$.
(b) [4 pt] Derive an expression for the total lifetime $t_{\rm univ}$ (Big Bang to Big Crunch) in terms of $H_0$ and $\Omega_{M,0}$.

(c) [4 pt] Assume that the universe is closed and expanding today. Derive an upper limit for $H_0$ using the fact that the current age of the Sun is $t_\odot$. Write this limit in terms of $\Omega_{M,0}$ and $t_\odot$.

finalAnswers.prompt: (b) with numbers: $\Omega_{M,0}=1.5$, $1/H_0=13.97$ Gyr. Lifetime in Gyr.
(c) with numbers: $\Omega_{M,0}=1.5$, $t_\odot=4.6$ Gyr. Upper limit on $H_0$ in km/s/Mpc.

keyPoints: (a) Big Bang $a=0$ at $\eta=0$; expansion slows; maximum (turnaround) at $\eta=\pi$; contraction to the Big Crunch $a=0$ at $\eta=2\pi$. Sketch: symmetric arch (cycloid), labelled points.
